question: Will Kerala health authorities have officially confirmed at least one 2026 measles death in Malappuram district as of October 2, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Two paths to YES: (a) the single already-pending suspected death (occurred ~August 2026) is upgraded to officially confirmed by Oct 2, or (b) a new Malappuram measles death occurs AND is officially confirmed inside the remaining ~11 days. Path (a) requires a formal Kerala death audit plus lab attribution to complete in a narrow window; the death has already sat in 'suspected' status for roughly 4-6 weeks as of Sept 21, and Indian state death-audit committees typically take weeks-to-months, with a substantial share of suspected deaths never reclassified as confirmed. Path (b) is small: ~400+ estimated infections at a 1-3/1000 CFR implies well under one expected death over the whole outbreak, so an 11-day slice carries a low occurrence probability, and same-window official confirmation is rarer still. The question's fine print explicitly excludes 'suspected'/'awaiting death audit' status, which is exactly the current state. Offsetting upward: high political salience (district collector task force Sept 21, district-wide alert) can force a definitive public statement, the criteria tolerate late-published confirmation of a status that existed by Oct 2, and I could not read the IDSP PDF to rule out a district-attributable measles death already sitting in the statewide row. Evidence is thin and one-sided toward status quo, so I stay near the base rate for a bureaucratic confirmation landing in a specified short window.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off an OFFICIAL Kerala government health-authority confirmation (Kerala DHS / district health authority) that a 2026 death in Malappuram district was attributed to measles, reported by credible media or appearing in an official Kerala report such as the IDSP daily communicable-diseases report (https://dhs.kerala.gov.in/en/idsp-2). It does NOT resolve off case counts, off a death labelled 'suspected', 'under investigation', or 'awaiting death audit / lab confirmation', and not off a statewide IDSP measles death figure unless that death is specifically identified as Malappuram (via report notes or accompanying official statements).

EVENT WINDOW: death must have occurred during calendar year 2026 and confirmation must exist as of end of October 2, 2026 IST -> window 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-02 IST (275 days); as of Now (2026-09-21T22:22Z = 2026-09-22 03:52 IST) approximately 96% elapsed, leaving about 11 days for a confirmation to be issued. The criteria state the question is not annulled by a late-publishing source: a confirmation status existing by Oct 2 but reported afterwards still governs.

EVIDENCE BULLETS:
- OnManorama, 2026-09-18: Malappuram has 63 laboratory-confirmed measles cases in 2026; health officials estimate actual infections have crossed 400. Valavannur health block accounts for 74 confirmed-plus-suspected cases; spread also in Athavanad, Kalpakanchery and other pockets.
- OnManorama, 2026-09-18: 'Authorities are also investigating one suspected death linked to the virus, though this has not yet been officially confirmed.' No death-audit finding is described in that report.
- ETHealthworld (Economic Times), 2026-09-21: 98 suspected fever-and-rash cases reported this month, six laboratory-confirmed in Valavannur and neighbouring Athavanad, Kalpakanchery, Thanaloor; 'one death reported last month is suspected to be linked to the disease' — i.e. the death occurred in approximately August 2026 and remained suspected as of 2026-09-21.
- ETHealthworld, 2026-09-21: Malappuram DMO Dr Vinod V states nearly 70% of cases are children who had not received MMR; mosques asked to carry vaccination messages, schools to hold special assemblies, vaccination camps under way.
- OnManorama, 2026-09-18: a district task force meeting chaired by the District Collector was scheduled for 2026-09-21 to streamline emergency control measures; a district-wide alert was under consideration. No public readout of that meeting was retrievable as of Now.
- Kerala DHS IDSP index page (checked Now): daily reports are published through 2026-09-18; cadence is daily, so roughly 11-13 further editions fall inside the window. The report's standing note: reported cases and deaths are preliminary and 'liable to change after Lab tests and Death audits'.
- The Sept 18 IDSP PDF was fetched this run but returned unparseable binary; the statewide Measles row values (2026 cumulative suspected cases, confirmed cases, deaths) were NOT read. Whether a non-zero statewide 2026 measles death is already listed is UNVERIFIED.
- Per the question background, the IDSP district-wise section does not break measles deaths out by district; district attribution historically appears via report notes or official statements to the press.
- Death-audit mechanics: Kerala operates a formal death-audit process (DHS death-audit government order, 2021). Comparable Indian practice (Karnataka dengue, Deccan Herald reporting) shows suspected deaths withheld from the confirmed column until a state audit committee sits, with multi-month gaps, and a share of audited deaths classified 'unconfirmed' rather than confirmed.
- Prior outbreak comparator: Malappuram 2023 measles outbreak recorded 1,304 confirmed cases and three deaths (deaths were eventually officially attributed). The lag between each 2023 death and its official attribution could NOT be established this run.
- Case-fatality reference: measles CFR commonly cited at roughly 1-3 per 1,000 cases where health-care access is reasonable; applied to the ~400+ estimated infections this gives an expected 2026 outbreak death count below one, with wide uncertainty; higher CFRs apply in malnourished or unvaccinated-infant subgroups, and ~70% of current cases are unvaccinated children.
- Competing local context: a flash flood at Pookkottumpadam / T.K. Colony in Malappuram killed at least five people on 2026-09-20/21, drawing the District Collector, the Revenue Minister and the Chief Minister to the district and dominating Malappuram news coverage in the days immediately before Now.
- Market check: no contract on this event found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or any bookmaker (harness title search plus own search) — 'no market found', so no external price is available.

STATUS QUO OUTCOME: no officially confirmed 2026 Malappuram measles death exists as of Now; the one known candidate death remains classified as suspected/under investigation.

BASE RATES FOUND:
- Over Indian-state suspected infectious-disease deaths pending a formal audit committee: confirmation typically lags weeks-to-months from the date of death, and a material fraction are audited into a non-confirmed category (Karnataka dengue audit reporting, Deccan Herald; Kerala IDSP 'liable to change after Death audits' note). No published numeric Kerala-specific conversion rate or turnaround distribution was locatable.
- Over measles cases generally: ~1-3 deaths per 1,000 cases with reasonable health-care access (WHO-style figure cited in the question background); over the 2023 Malappuram outbreak specifically: 3 deaths / 1,304 confirmed cases = ~2.3 per 1,000 confirmed cases.
- Conditional on the present outbreak's scale (63 lab-confirmed, >400 estimated infections), the 2023 per-confirmed-case rate implies well under one death and the per-estimated-infection rate implies on the order of one death across the full outbreak to date.
